body: Australia Post: Your parcel could not be delivered. Pay a $2.95 redelivery fee within 24 hours or it will be returned to sender.
redFlags: Comes from a random mobile number, not an official channel
Urgent 24 hour deadline
Asks for a payment through a link
Link domain is not the real Australia Post domain
explanation: Delivery scams use small fees to steal card details. If you are expecting a parcel, open the official app or website and enter the tracking number yourself.

subject: Action required: your myGov account has been locked
body: We detected unusual activity on your myGov account. To avoid permanent suspension, verify your identity within 12 hours by logging in below.
redFlags: Sender domain has extra words like 'secure-login'
Threatens suspension to create panic
Asks you to log in through an email link
Short deadline
explanation: Government services do not ask you to verify your identity through email links. Type the official address into your browser or use the official app instead.

body: Your toll invoice is overdue. Pay now to avoid a $150 late fee and possible licence suspension.
redFlags: Does not name the toll company or your vehicle
Threatens a big fee and licence suspension
Generic link with no real company domain
Unknown mobile number
explanation: Real toll notices usually include specific trip details and point you to the official site or app. Vague, threatening texts with a payment link are a classic scam.

subject: Your receipt for October
body: Thanks for being Premium. Your payment of $13.99 was successful. No action is needed.
safeSigns: No link asking you to log in
Tells you no action is needed
explanation: This is a plain receipt. It asks you to do nothing and does not push you to click. If you are unsure, check your subscription inside the app.

subject: Your password expires today
body: Your university password will expire in 3 hours. Click below to keep your password and avoid losing access to email and Moodle.
redFlags: Sender domain is not the real university domain
Short deadline of 3 hours
Asks you to enter your password through a link
Threatens loss of access
explanation: Students are a common target for credential theft. Real password resets are done through the official university portal, not through links in surprise emails.

subject: Free pizza at the Cyber Club meetup, Thursday 5pm
body: Come along to our first meetup of the semester. Room details are on the events page. No RSVP needed, just show up.
safeSigns: No login or personal details requested
Normal, expected content from a student club
explanation: This is an ordinary event notice. It does not ask for money, passwords or clicks. Not every email is a scam, and learning to relax on safe ones matters too.

subject: 2 bed apartment, $320/week, near campus
body: Hi! I'm overseas for work so I can't do inspections. Send a $500 holding deposit and I'll post you the keys. Many people are interested so please be quick.
redFlags: Price is far below the market rate
Owner is conveniently overseas
Wants a deposit before any inspection
Pressure from other interested people
explanation: Fake rental listings target students looking for housing. Never pay a deposit before seeing the property, and check listings through trusted agents.

body: omg is this you in this video?? 😭 so embarrassing
redFlags: Out-of-character message with no context
Emotional hook to make you click fast
Link goes to a site that is not Instagram
Likely a hacked account, even though the sender is a real friend
explanation: Scammers hijack accounts and message the owner's friends. Message your friend on another app to check, and never log in through a link someone sends.

body: We noticed a card payment of $84.20 at a store you don't usually shop at. If this wasn't you, open the YourBank app and review your recent transactions.
safeSigns: Tells you to open the app yourself, not click a link
No request for passwords, PINs or codes
Gives a specific transaction you can verify in your own app
explanation: Real bank alerts send you to your own app and never ask for sensitive details by text. Even so, check the transaction in the app rather than replying.

subject: Job offer: Remote Admin Assistant, $45/hr
body: Congratulations, you are hired with no interview needed. To set up payroll, send your bank details and ID photo. We will also send a cheque for equipment. Please buy gift cards for the supplies and send us the codes.
redFlags: Hired without an interview or application
Pay is unusually high for the work
Asks for bank details and ID upfront
Gift cards and cheque for equipment is a known scam pattern
explanation: Job scams often target students who need work. A real employer will not ask you to buy gift cards or pay for supplies out of your own pocket.
